repos.brief:
**What it does:** REA is a TypeScript MCP server that connects AI agents to reverse-engineering tools (Hopper, Ghidra, IDA, static JS analysis) so they can inspect native binaries, Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites without source code.

**Why now:** The repo hit #1 trending on GitHub this week, gaining over 61,000 stars in seven days, signaling a sharp spike in builder attention around agent-driven binary analysis.

**Build with it:** Run `npx rea-agents setup`, point it at an existing Ghidra installation, and wire it into Claude or Codex to let your agent decompile and explain a closed-source feature before you reimplement it.

**What it does:** A structured, 523-lesson curriculum (Python, TypeScript, Rust, Julia) for implementing AI model internals, retrieval pipelines, and agent runtimes from scratch, with runnable local labs and built-in evaluations.

**Why now:** The repo gained nearly 37,000 stars in a single week, signaling a sharp surge in community attention that makes it a timely reference for builders orienting around the current AI engineering skill stack.

**Build with it:** Pick the agents or transformers phase, run the local lab code, and use the included test harness to inspect failure modes in your own retrieval pipeline.

**What it does:** HyperFrames is an open-source TypeScript framework that converts HTML, CSS, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos via Chrome's BeginFrame API, operable through a CLI, AI agent skills, or a hosted authoring workflow.

**Why now:** The repo gained 35,000 stars this week alongside HN threads covering both its Chrome BeginFrame rendering approach and its agent-native skill system, marking a clear breakout moment for the project.

**Build with it:** Wire it into Claude Code by running `claude plugin marketplace add heygen-com/hyperframes` and then invoking `/hyperframes` to let the agent plan, lint, and render an HTML-based video without leaving your editor.

**What it does:** Scrapling is a Python web-scraping framework that handles adaptive element tracking, stealth fetching via Playwright, and full-scale crawling under a single API.

**Why now:** The repo gained 24,823 stars in a single week, signaling a viral adoption spike that makes it a live community resource worth evaluating before the ecosystem consolidates around it.

**Build with it:** Point Scrapling's `StealthyFetcher` at a bot-protected page and replace your existing `requests` + BeautifulSoup pipeline to validate whether its auto-adapting selectors survive a real anti-bot challenge.

**What it does:** A 677-item, evidence-graded life-optimization guide for mainland China covering health, finance, law, social insurance, and business compliance, with every entry citing peer-reviewed journals or official documents and specifying cost, benefit, and evidence level.

**Why now:** The repo gained 15,346 stars this week, signaling a viral discovery moment that surfaces a ready-made structured dataset and AI skill layer worth examining before the wave passes.

**Build with it:** Install the included Claude Code / Codex skill (`skills/life-decision-guide/`) and query it against your own decision context—e.g., "签担保合同该注意什么"—to see how a citation-anchored retrieval skill is structured, then adapt that skill pattern to your own domain corpus.

**What it does:** UI UX Pro Max is a Python-based AI skill that injects 192 reasoning rules and 79 searchable UI styles into AI coding tools (Cursor, Windsurf, Claude Code, Copilot) to guide professional UI/UX output across React, Tailwind, and mobile frameworks.

**Why now:** The repo crossed 134K stars with 1,700+ added this week, signaling a sharp spike in builder adoption across the AI-editor ecosystem.

**Build with it:** Install the `ui-ux-pro-max-cli` npm package and point it at your Cursor or Windsurf project to immediately activate the style and reasoning rules during code generation.

**What it does:** PPT Master takes a PDF, DOCX, or web page as input and outputs a natively editable PPTX file complete with shapes, transitions, animations, charts, tables, and optional audio narration from speaker notes.

**Why now:** The project gained 1,639 stars this week and its primary sponsor just launched Kimi K3, a 3-trillion-parameter open model with a 1-million-token context window that PPT Master explicitly targets for document-to-slide conversion.

**Build with it:** Point PPT Master at the Kimi Open Platform API and your own `.pptx` template file to generate on-brand decks from long-form documents without touching slide layout manually.

**What it does:** Hermes Agent is a self-improving AI agent with a closed learning loop — it creates and refines skills from experience, searches past sessions via FTS5, and builds a persistent user model using Honcho dialectic modeling, deployable across CLI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, and serverless backends like Modal or Daytona.

**Why now:** The repo crossed 252k stars with 1,543 added this week, signaling a sharp spike in builder attention around its serverless-persistence model and open skill standard at agentskills.io.

**Build with it:** Point it at your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint via `hermes model`, then trigger the skill-creation loop on a complex task to see autonomous skill generation and cross-session recall in action without any code changes.

**What it does:** Caveman is a prompt-engineering toolkit — a slash skill (`/caveman`, `/ultracave`, `/megacave`) plus an LLM proxy — that rewrites agent output in stripped-down "caveman English," cutting input tokens by ~33% and output cost by 1.4–2.4× with no change to code or commands.

**Why now:** The project hit #1 on Hacker News this week and was A/B tested by JetBrains, who published results showing measurable token savings across real agent workflows.

**Build with it:** Drop the `/caveman` skill file into your Claude Code project's `.claude/commands/` folder and run a cost comparison against your current baseline using the proxy's built-in token logging.

**What it does:** Awesome-Selfhosted is a curated directory of free-software network services and web applications you can host on your own servers, spanning analytics, CMS, email, file transfer, CRM, and dozens of other categories.

**Why now:** The repo gained 1,393 stars this week, a notable spike that signals fresh builder interest in self-hosted alternatives amid ongoing SaaS pricing and privacy pressures.

**Build with it:** Pick a category matching a dependency you currently pay for (e.g., analytics or email), fork the HTML version at awesome-selfhosted.net, and use it as a shortlist to evaluate drop-in replacements against your existing stack.
